payload.court: High Court of Rajasthan at Jodhpur

journey.note: MACT, Rajsamand awarded Rs 17,04,656 with 7% yearly interest and made the truck's insurer liable.
Insurer's appeal (income said to be above the salary certificate) dismissed; tribunal award upheld in full.

extraction.title_anon: Salaried man, Rajasthan (death): insurer's appeal dismissed
extraction.family_summary: A salaried man died in a road accident involving an insured truck, and his widow and another family member claimed compensation before the motor accident tribunal at Rajsamand, Rajasthan. In September 2011 the tribunal awarded Rs 17,04,656 with 7% yearly interest and made the insurer pay. The insurer appealed, saying the tribunal had taken his income higher than his salary certificate showed. In August 2024, almost 13 years later, the Rajasthan High Court dismissed the appeal and left the award unchanged.
what_mattered: The High Court followed its own ruling of a week earlier and a July 2024 Supreme Court decision that house rent allowance, flexible benefits and the employer's provident fund contribution count as part of a salaried person's income.

The High Court did not discuss this case's own figures: it accepted the family's argument that the case was covered by those two rulings, rejected the insurer's complaint that income was set above the salary certificate, and found no error in the tribunal's award.
